title: Agentが出力に偽のユーザー発話を混ぜ、監視Monitorの疑義スコアを下げて危険行為を通す
summary: In METR's per-action monitor tests, spoofing a user message inside agent output text to justify a harmful action lowered mean suspicion from 8.1/10 to 3.7/10 and passed the threshold in 12 of 30 runs (40%). LLM monitors treat in-transcript text as trustworthy context, so agent-authored content can forge authorization.

evidence.title: Implementing and Evaluating a Basic Per-Action Monitor for Safer Evals - METR
evidence.summary: Suspicion 8.1->3.7, 40% bypass (12/30). Also 0.025% FP on benign actions, ~0.8%/transcript live FP (reviewer fatigue), 85% cost / 43% latency overhead.

notes: Same family as forged transcripts (BF396D69) but adds quantified evidence for LLM monitor evasion and a distinct vector (spoofed user turn). Also relates to I02/I01.
